scopeNote: Specialty (third-wave) coffee shops and roasters: 16 on Phuket (Old Town, Patong, Kata, Rawai, Chalong, Kamala, Bang Tao), 4 on Koh Phangan, 2 on Koh Samui, 1 in Ao Nang (Krabi) and 1 in Khao Lak.

basics.title: Coffee in Thailand
basics.text: Thailand grows its own coffee: arabica in the northern hills of Chiang Rai, Chiang Mai and Nan (Doi Chang and Doi Tung are the best known names), and robusta in the south, mostly around Chumphon, Surat Thani and Ranong. A Thai iced coffee is sweet by default, with sugar and condensed milk: say 'wan noi' (less sweet) or 'mai sai nam tan' (no sugar), or order an Americano or a pour-over in a specialty shop. In 2026 a specialty espresso drink costs about 80-130 THB and a pour-over or signature drink 100-180 THB; a sweet iced coffee from a street stall is about 40-60 THB.

items.praise: The name every Phuket coffee list starts with: The Way to Coffee (Nov 2025) calls it the place to begin, and the Thai Holiday Guide (Jul 2026, facts checked Oct 2026) puts it first. It roasts its own beans, mostly from northern Thailand, and came fifth at the International Coffee Roast Master Thailand 2019 (Daniel Food Diary).
items.watchOut: Small and often full by mid morning.
items.description: A small-batch roaster with an espresso bar and a slow bar in an old pharmacy building in the Old Town. It started with a university student roasting at home.
tips: For drip coffee they ask Thai or imported bean: try the Thai one.
Bags of their beans are on sale at the counter.
There is a second shop in north Patong, 300 m from the Patong villa.
